LESSON: READING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Reading 2.1 Reading Aloud: Fluency (2 sessions) • Pronunciation • Simple sentenc
Topic 2.4: Reading for Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading for Comprehension, part of Reading 2.1 Reading Aloud: Fluency (2 sessions) • Pronunciation • Simple sentenc in Grade 7 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How can we derive the meaning of a new word in texts?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to read simple sentences in a text and circle familiar words and phrases,

2. pick out vocabulary from a text related to the theme,

3. build a vocabulary bank on the words identified from the text,

4. work jointly to infer meaning of words from context,

5. use the vocabulary acquired to make sentences.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to read simple sentences in a text and circle familiar words and phrases,
2. pick out vocabulary from a text related to the theme,
3. build a vocabulary bank on the words identified from the text,
4. work jointly to infer meaning of words from context,
5. use the vocabulary acquired to make sentences.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading for Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: The learner exhibits a self-directed intention to learn when working jointly to infer the meaning of words

from context.

• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: Evaluation and decision-making skills are enhanced as learners work with peers to

read simple sentences in a text and circle familiar words and phrases.

Values:
Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner engages in assigned duties when building a vocabulary bank on the words

identified from the text.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social Cohesion: This is promoted as learners interact with vocabulary related to the theme of family and appreciate the place

of the family institution in promoting co-existence.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept on family to concepts of social organisation as covered in Social Studies.
